description: Parameters of the EAGLE 9.6 SET command from the built-in help (SET, Configuring EAGLE, ROUTE, ROUTEMULTI, DRC, Selection Filter and related topics): snapping and selection, menu contents, context menus, wire bend styles, colors and fill styles, display options, editing modes, automatic confirmation of dialogs (important for scripts), file locking, routing and ripup modes, panel toggles and the eaglerc parameters that can only be changed with SET. Settings are typically put into eagle.scr or a script; most are stored in the eaglerc user file.

tools.name: SET
tools.description: Changes program parameters that affect behavior, screen display and user interface of the editors. Without parameters it opens the settings dialog (Options/Set); with a keyword and value it changes one setting, which makes it the standard way to configure EAGLE from eagle.scr or other scripts. Any keyword that is not one of the documented SET options is looked up among the eaglerc parameters, so practically every eaglerc entry can be changed with SET.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Keyword and value(s), e.g. WIRE_BEND 2, CONFIRM YES, POLYGON_RATSNEST OFF (see the individual SET entries).

parameters.name: eaglerc parameter
parameters.description: Any eaglerc parameter written in full and case sensitive, typically with value 0 (off) or 1 (on), e.g. Option.ViaLength.

tools.notes: After changing a display-related eaglerc parameter a window refresh (WINDOW;) may be needed. eagle -U- starts without reading or writing the eaglerc settings file. Keywords can be abbreviated and are not case sensitive (eaglerc parameter names are). Related: GRID, MENU, ASSIGN, CHANGE (presets for new objects), SCRIPT.

tools.name: SET SNAP_LENGTH
tools.description: Limit distance for the snap function: ROUTE snaps to same-signal target objects (e.g. off-grid pads) within this distance regardless of the grid, and NET snaps net ends to pin tips within it. Value in the current unit.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Snap radius in the current GRID unit. Default: 20 mil.

tools.notes: A snapped target is shown with an X in ROUTE and with a small circle at the pin tip in NET. Related: ROUTE, NET.

tools.name: SET CATCH_FACTOR
tools.description: Maximum distance from the cursor within which objects are considered when clicking, relative to the height or width (whichever is smaller) of the visible part of the drawing. It applies at zoom levels showing at least 4 inches and grows logarithmically when zooming in further.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Values < 1 are factors, values >= 1 are percent; 0 turns the limit off. Default: 0.05 (5%).

tools.notes: Related: SET SELECT_FACTOR, Selection Filter.

tools.name: SET SELECT_FACTOR
tools.description: Distance from the cursor within which nearby objects are suggested for selection, relative to the height or width (whichever is smaller) of the visible part of the drawing.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Values < 1 are factors, values >= 1 are percent. Default: 0.02 (2%).

tools.notes: Related: SET CATCH_FACTOR, SET SELECTTYPES / SELECTLAYERS.

tools.name: SET USED_LAYERS
tools.description: Specifies which layers appear in the layer menus of the editors (e.g. the DISPLAY menu). Pads, Vias, Unrouted, Dimension, Drills and Holes, the schematic layers and all signal layers in use always remain in the menus.

parameters.name: name | number
parameters.description: Layer name or number; All activates all layers.

tools.notes: The help refers to the example script mylayers.scr (in the EAGLE 9.6 installation under examples/scripts/examples), which also sets layer colors and fill styles. Related: DISPLAY, LAYER.

tools.name: SET WIDTH_MENU, DIAMETER_MENU, DRILL_MENU, SMD_MENU, SIZE_MENU, ISOLATE_MENU, SPACING_MENU, MITER_MENU, ROUTERADIUS_MENU
tools.description: Configure the values offered in the popup menus of the parameter toolbars: wire width, pad/via diameter, drill, smd size, text size, polygon isolate and spacing, miter radius and the radius used by the arc routing modes. Setting your standard values makes interactive work faster and consistent.

parameters.name: value..
parameters.description: Up to 16 values per menu (16 value pairs for SMD_MENU); the help examples set the GRID unit first, so values are given in the current unit.

parameters.name: (no values)
parameters.description: SET WIDTH_MENU; (etc.) restores the program defaults.

tools.notes: ROUTERADIUS_MENU is listed under routing modes ('Radius For Arc Modes'). Related: CHANGE WIDTH / DIAMETER / DRILL / SMD / SIZE / ISOLATE / SPACING, MITER.

tools.name: SET DLINE_WIDTH_MENU, DLINE_EXT_WIDTH_MENU, DLINE_EXT_LENGTH_MENU, DLINE_EXT_OFFSET_MENU
tools.description: Configure the popup menu values for dimension objects: dimension line width and the extension line width, length and offset, which correspond to the parameters of CHANGE DLINE.

parameters.name: value..
parameters.description: Up to 16 values; without values the defaults are restored.

tools.notes: Related: DIMENSION, CHANGE DLINE width [ extension_width [ extension_length [ extension_offset ]]].

tools.name: SET CONTEXT
tools.description: Adds user-defined entries to the right-click context menus of selectable object types; each entry has a menu text and a command sequence executed when it is clicked, typically RUN of a ULP. Entries are stored in eaglerc, their number is unlimited, and existing user entries can be overwritten.

parameters.name: objecttype
parameters.description: attribute, circle, dimension, element, frame, gate, hole, instance, junction, label, modinst, pad, pin, rectangle, smd, text, via, wire (not case sensitive).

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Menu text; enclose in single quotes if it contains blanks (inner quotes doubled).

parameters.name: commands
parameters.description: Command sequence to execute, in single quotes if it contains blanks.

parameters.name: SET CONTEXT objecttype; / SET CONTEXT;
parameters.description: Delete all user entries of that object type / all user-defined entries.

tools.notes: For a ULP to see the clicked object via ingroup(), do not put a ';' inside the quoted command ('run myexport.ulp', not 'run myexport.ulp;'). Related: RUN.

tools.name: SET WIRE_BEND
tools.description: Selects the bend style used by commands that draw wires and lines (LINE, NET, BUS, ROUTE, POLYGON, SPLIT ...), and optionally restricts which styles the right mouse button cycles through. Styles 8 and 9 are the follow-me router modes that route airwire ends automatically.

parameters.description: Start - horizontal - vertical - end.
Start - horizontal - 45 degrees - end.
Start - end (straight connection).
Start - 45 degrees - horizontal - end.
Start - vertical - horizontal - end.
Start - arc - horizontal - end.
Start - horizontal - arc - end.
'Freehand' (arc fitting the wire at the start, straight otherwise).
Route the short end of the airwire with the follow-me router.
Route both ends of the airwire with the follow-me router.

parameters.name: @ bend_nr ...
parameters.description: Styles used when switching with the right mouse button; '@' alone restores all.

tools.notes: Styles 0, 1, 3 and 4 may contain additional miter wires (see MITER). While drawing, Right switches styles, Shift+Right reverses, Ctrl+Right toggles corresponding styles.

tools.name: SET BEEP
tools.description: Switches the acoustic signal (beep) of the editor on or off.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable the beep.

tools.notes: The help uses this parameter as its example of alternative parameters in the command syntax description.

tools.name: SET GROUP_ANNOTATIONS
tools.description: Controls whether persistent (NEWGROUP) groups show their boundary and title annotations in the schematic: always, never, or only while the mouse pointer is inside the group bounds.

parameters.name: OFF
parameters.description: Annotations never shown.

parameters.name: ON
parameters.description: Annotations always shown.

parameters.name: HOVERONLY
parameters.description: Shown when the pointer is within the group bounds (spelled HOVER_ONLY in the Design Manager help).

tools.notes: The same setting is stored as eaglerc parameter Sch.GroupAnnotations (0 off, 1 on, 2 hover only). Annotations can also be switched off per group in its properties. Related: NEWGROUP, EDITGROUP, UNGROUP.

tools.name: SET COLOR_LAYER and SET COLOR_GRID
tools.description: Set the display color of a layer or of the grid lines, using a palette color number or name. Useful in eagle.scr or a color script to get the same layer colors on every machine.
tools.usage:
SET COLOR_LAYER layer color;
SET COLOR_GRID color;

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Layer number or name.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Palette index or name: 0 Black, 1 Blue, 2 Green, 3 Cyan, 4 Red, 5 Magenta, 6 Brown, 7 LGray, 8 DGray, 9 LBlue, 10 LGreen, 11 LCyan, 12 LRed, 13 LMagenta, 14 Yellow, 15 White (default palette entries 0..15; up to 63 with SET PALETTE).

tools.notes: Colors 0..7 are 'normal' colors and 8..15 their 'highlight' versions (same scheme for 16..31 etc.); highlight colors are used e.g. by SHOW. The shipped example mylayers.scr sets all layer colors. Related: SET PALETTE, SET FILL_LAYER, DISPLAY.

tools.name: SET FILL_LAYER
tools.description: Sets the fill style used for wires, rectangles and other filled objects of a layer on screen (and in PRINT unless SOLID is used).

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Layer number or name.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Name or number: 0 Empty, 1 Solid, 2 Line, 3 LtSlash, 4 Slash, 5 BkSlash, 6 LtBkSlash, 7 Hatch, 8 XHatch, 9 Interleave, 10 WideDot, 11 CloseDot, 12 Stipple1, 13 Stipple2, 14 Stipple3, 15 Stipple4.

tools.notes: Related: SET COLOR_LAYER, SET DRC_FILL, PRINT SOLID.

tools.name: SET PALETTE
tools.description: Edits the color palettes or switches between them. There are three palettes (black, white and colored background), each with 64 ARGB entries; entry 0 is the background color. The white palette is also used for printing, so its background entry cannot be changed.
tools.usage:
SET PALETTE index argb
SET PALETTE BLACK|WHITE|COLORED

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Palette entry 0..63.

parameters.name: argb
parameters.description: Hexadecimal value starting with 0x, e.g. 0xFFFFFF00 (bright yellow); alpha 0x00 = fully transparent, 0xFF = opaque; the background alpha is always 0xFF.

parameters.name: BLACK | WHITE | COLORED
parameters.description: Switch to the black, white or colored background palette.

tools.notes: There is no automatic refresh after SET PALETTE; follow it with WINDOW;. Without the 0x prefix the value is read as decimal. By default only entries 0..15 are used. Also editable in Options/Set.../Colors.

tools.name: SET MIN_GRID_SIZE
tools.description: The grid is drawn only if the grid spacing on screen is larger than this number of pixels, which avoids a cluttered view when zoomed out.

parameters.name: pixels
parameters.description: Minimum on-screen grid spacing in pixels.

tools.notes: The WINDOW help mentions the related dialog setting Options/Set/Misc 'Min. visible grid size', which decides whether the finest grid can be seen at maximum zoom. Related: GRID, WINDOW.

tools.name: SET MIN_TEXT_SIZE
tools.description: Texts smaller than this height in pixels are drawn as rectangles on the screen to speed up display; 0 draws all texts readably.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Height in pixels; 0 = always draw text.

tools.notes: Only affects the screen display. Related: TEXT.

tools.name: SET NET_WIRE_WIDTH and SET BUS_WIRE_WIDTH
tools.description: Line widths used by the NET and BUS commands for new net and bus wires in schematics.
tools.usage:
SET NET_WIRE_WIDTH width;
SET BUS_WIRE_WIDTH width;

parameters.name: NET_WIRE_WIDTH width
parameters.description: Net wire width. Default: 6 mil.

parameters.name: BUS_WIRE_WIDTH width
parameters.description: Bus wire width. Default: 30 mil.

tools.notes: The 'Configuring EAGLE' help page lists these as SET NET_LINE_WIDTH and SET BUS_LINE_WIDTH, while the SET, NET and BUS pages use NET_WIRE_WIDTH and BUS_WIRE_WIDTH. Related: NET, BUS.

tools.name: SET DISPLAY_MODE and SET PAD_NAMES
tools.description: Pad display options: DISPLAY_MODE REAL shows pads as they will be plotted, NODRILL shows pads (and vias) without drill holes, which also makes PRINT output them filled. PAD_NAMES shows or hides pad names in footprints and boards.
tools.usage:
SET DISPLAY_MODE REAL | NODRILL;
SET PAD_NAMES OFF | ON;

parameters.name: REAL
parameters.description: Pads displayed as they will be plotted.

parameters.name: NODRILL
parameters.description: Pads shown without drill hole.

parameters.name: PAD_NAMES OFF | ON
parameters.description: Hide / display pad names.

tools.notes: Related: PAD, VIA, PRINT.

tools.name: SET DRC_FILL
tools.description: Fill style of the error polygons that DRC draws to mark design rule violations.

parameters.name: fill_name
parameters.description: Fill style name or number as for SET FILL_LAYER. Default: LtSlash.

tools.notes: Related: DRC, ERRORS, SET LIVE_DRC.

tools.name: SET POLYGON_RATSNEST
tools.description: Controls whether RATSNEST also calculates the signal polygons (real mode). Turning it off keeps polygons in the faster outline mode while airwires are recalculated.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: ON: RATSNEST calculates polygons (the behavior described in the RATSNEST and POLYGON help, which can be turned off); OFF: no polygon calculation.

tools.notes: The polygon calculation is what prevents airwires for pads already connected through a polygon, so with OFF such pads keep their airwires. The CAM Processor always calculates polygons. Related: POLYGON, RATSNEST, RIPUP @.

tools.name: SET VECTOR_FONT
tools.description: Sets the 'persistent in this drawing' vector font option of an existing board or schematic, so that all its texts are displayed and printed with the built-in vector font; the option is stored in the drawing and travels with it.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable forced vector font for the current drawing.

tools.notes: The user-level option 'Always vector font' is the eaglerc parameter Interface.VectorFont (SET Interface.VectorFont 0|1); its current value is copied into new drawings. The CAM Processor always uses the vector font. Related: TEXT, CHANGE FONT.

tools.name: SET XREF_LABEL_FORMAT
tools.description: Format string of cross-reference labels (LABEL with the XREF option) in schematics, which point to the next sheet where the net continues. The string is stored in the schematic file.

parameters.name: %F
parameters.description: Draw a flag border around the label.

parameters.name: %N
parameters.description: Net name.

parameters.name: %S / %C / %R
parameters.description: Next sheet number / column / row on that sheet (column and row need a frame).

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: '%F%N/%S.%C%R'; any other ASCII characters may be added.

tools.notes: Also set in Options/Set/Misc 'Xref label format'. Related: LABEL, FRAME, SET XREF_PART_FORMAT.

tools.name: SET XREF_PART_FORMAT
tools.description: Format string for part cross-references displayed by the text variable >XREF in symbols (e.g. relay contacts that refer to the coil's sheet position).

parameters.name: %S / %C / %R
parameters.description: Sheet number / column / row on the sheet.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: '/%S.%C%R'; other ASCII characters may be added.

tools.notes: Also set in Options/Set/Misc 'Xref part format'. Related: TEXT (>XREF, >CONTACT_XREF), FRAME.

tools.name: SET CHECK_CONNECTS
tools.description: Switches the check in ADD that every pin of a device has been connected to a pad with CONNECT. Even with the check off, no board can be generated from a schematic that contains a device without package.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable the connect check (the help describes it as a check that can be switched off).

tools.notes: Related: ADD, CONNECT, PACKAGE, BOARD.

tools.name: SET REPLACE_SAME
tools.description: Chooses how REPLACE matches footprints when only a board is edited (or for elements without a schematic part): by pad/smd names or by pad/smd coordinates.

parameters.name: NAMES
parameters.description: Default. The new footprint must have the same pad/smd names; positions do not matter; additional pads allowed.

parameters.name: COORDS
parameters.description: Pads/smds must be at the same coordinates relative to the origin; names may differ.

tools.example:
SET REPLACE_SAME COORDS;
REPLACE IC1 SO16W;
tools.notes: In both modes, pads connected to signals must exist in the new footprint. Related: REPLACE, UPDATE.

tools.name: SET UNDO_LOG
tools.description: Switches the undo buffer on or off. The buffer uses memory; turning it off disables UNDO and REDO.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable recording of undo steps (normally on; the help describes switching it off when memory is short).

tools.notes: Related: UNDO, REDO.

tools.name: SET OPTIMIZING
tools.description: When on, wires/lines that end up collinear after MOVE, ROUTE or SPLIT are merged automatically into a single wire. Turn it off when you want to keep split points, e.g. to give part of a track a different width.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable automatic joining (on unless disabled, according to the OPTIMIZE help).

tools.notes: The OPTIMIZE command works regardless of this setting. Related: OPTIMIZE, SPLIT, MOVE, ROUTE.

tools.name: SET AUTO_END_NET
tools.description: Automatic ending of nets and busses: when on, a net or bus wire placed on another net/bus wire or a pin ends there. Also 'Auto end net and bus' in Options/Set/Misc.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable automatic ending (enabled unless switched off, per the NET help).

tools.notes: Related: NET, BUS, SET AUTO_JUNCTION.

tools.name: SET AUTO_JUNCTION
tools.description: Automatic junctions: when on, a junction dot is placed where a net wire ends at a point with at least two other net wires and/or pins. Also 'Auto set junction' in Options/Set/Misc.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable automatic junctions (enabled unless switched off, per the NET help).

tools.notes: Related: JUNCTION, NET, ERC.

tools.name: SET CONFIRM
tools.description: Answers confirmation and message dialogs automatically, which is essential for unattended scripts: YES clicks the positive button (OK/Yes) without showing the dialog, NO the negative one (or just confirms if there is none), OPT1..OPT9 pick additional options such as the scope when renaming a net segment. OFF restores normal dialogs.
tools.usage: SET CONFIRM OFF | NO | YES | OPT1 | OPT2 | OPT3 | OPT4 | OPT5 | OPT6 | OPT7 | OPT8 | OPT9;

parameters.name: YES
parameters.description: Confirm every dialog positively.

parameters.name: NO
parameters.description: Choose 'No' where available, otherwise confirm.

parameters.name: OPT1..OPT9
parameters.description: Choose additional option n (e.g. OPT2 before NAME on a net segment).

parameters.name: OFF
parameters.description: Turn automatic confirmation off; it also falls back to OFF automatically at the next interactive input.

tools.notes: Do not put SET CONFIRM YES at the start of a script and run everything silently; wrap only the individual commands that need it, because blindly confirmed messages can hide important warnings.

tools.name: SET LOCKING
tools.description: Switches EAGLE's file locking: files loaded in a drawing editor or the text editor are normally locked for writing with a lock file named .file.lck. The change takes effect immediately (locks of open files are removed or created) and is stored in eaglerc.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable creating own locks (locking is on by default).

tools.notes: With locking off, EAGLE still respects locks of other users. When a locked file is opened you can save under another name, retry, delete or ignore the lock (then save under a different name). Not applicable to the CAM Processor and read-only files. Also in Control Panel Options / 'Backup / Locking'.

tools.name: SET LIC_WIDTH and SET LIC_HEIGHT
tools.description: For the Make Pro Edition only, whose board area is limited but can have variable width and height: setting one dimension adjusts the other accordingly.
tools.usage:
SET LIC_WIDTH width
SET LIC_HEIGHT height

parameters.name: width / height
parameters.description: Allowed board width or height; the other dimension follows.

tools.notes: Only meaningful with a Make Pro license (see EAGLE Editions); irrelevant for other editions. The help does not state the unit of the value (presumably the current GRID unit), so check the result in the dialog.

tools.name: SET LIVE_DRC
tools.description: Enables or disables Live DRC, which checks the design rules continuously while you edit the board instead of only when DRC is run.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable design rule checking while editing.

tools.notes: Related: DRC, SET DRC_FILL, ERRORS.

tools.name: SET SINGLE_LAYER_MODE
tools.description: With single layer mode active during routing, all layers except the active one are greyed out for a more focused view.

parameters.name: OFF | ON | TOGGLE
parameters.description: Disable, enable or toggle (TOGGLE listed in 'Configuring EAGLE'; the ROUTE help shows ON | OFF).

tools.notes: Related: ROUTE, DISPLAY.

tools.name: SET DESIGN_MANAGER, SET INSPECTOR, SET SELECTION_FILTER, SET SHEETS (panels)
tools.description: Show, hide or toggle the editor panels: Design Manager, Inspector (properties and attributes of the selection), Selection Filter and the Sheets panel of the schematic. Handy to assign to keys with ASSIGN.

parameters.name: OFF | ON | TOGGLE
parameters.description: Hide, show or toggle the panel.

tools.example:
SET INSPECTOR ON;
ASSIGN C+F9 'SET DESIGN_MANAGER TOGGLE;';
tools.notes: Related: SET SELECTTYPES / SELECTLAYERS, Design Manager, Inspector, Sheets panel.

tools.name: SET SELECTTYPES and SET SELECTLAYERS
tools.description: Configure the Selection Filter: SELECTTYPES restricts which object types can be selected (e.g. only wires and vias), SELECTLAYERS restricts selection to certain layers without changing their visibility. This removes ambiguity when clicking in dense designs.
tools.usage:
SET SELECTTYPES type.. ;
SET SELECTLAYERS layer.. ;

parameters.name: SELECTTYPES
parameters.description: Object type names (e.g. HOLE WIRE VIA); ALL selects all, a leading '-' removes a type (ALL -AIRWIRE).

parameters.name: SELECTLAYERS
parameters.description: Layer names/numbers; NONE clears first; presets such as PRESET_TOP can be used.

tools.notes: The examples are those given in the Selection Filter help. Related: SET SELECTION_FILTER, GROUP.

tools.name: SET MOVE_MODE
tools.description: Behavior of MOVE for wires and objects connected to wires: Preserve Angles keeps the original wire angles (with Ctrl, non-orthogonal wires snap to the grid), Free just follows the mouse, and Disconnect detaches the selected objects from their connections, e.g. to re-route a subcircuit without disturbing the rest.

parameters.name: PRESERVE_ANGLES
parameters.description: Maintain the original angles of connected wires.

parameters.name: FREE
parameters.description: No angle preservation.

parameters.name: DISCONNECT
parameters.description: Disconnect the selection from pads, vias, wires ...

tools.notes: Also selectable in the MOVE parameter toolbar. Related: MOVE.

tools.name: SET OBSTACLE_MODE
tools.description: Obstacle handling of the interactive router (ROUTE, ROUTEDIFF, ROUTEMULTI): ignore obstacles, walk around them following the design rules, or push movable obstacles aside (push and shove).

parameters.name: IGNORE
parameters.description: No design rule checks while routing; beware of shorts.

parameters.name: WALKAROUND
parameters.description: Default. Route around obstacles, legal via positions.

parameters.name: PUSH
parameters.description: Push movable objects aside, also around new vias.

tools.notes: Same as the Obstacle Avoidance icons in the ROUTE parameter toolbar. Related: ROUTE.

tools.name: SET LOOP_REMOVAL
tools.description: Loop removal in ROUTE: re-routing part of an existing path automatically deletes the redundant old loop of wires and vias.

parameters.name: OFF | ON
parameters.description: Disable / enable loop removal. Default: ON.

tools.notes: Does not work if the loop contains a component pad or the wires form a T-junction; not implemented for ROUTEDIFF and ROUTEMULTI. Related: ROUTE.

tools.name: SET VIA_PATTERN
tools.description: Arrangement of the vias that ROUTEMULTI places when several parallel tracks change layer together.
tools.usage: SET VIA_PATTERN PERPENDICULAR | ANGLE_RIGHT | ANGLE_LEFT | STAGGER;

parameters.name: PERPENDICULAR
parameters.description: Default: vias in a row perpendicular to the route direction.

parameters.name: ANGLE_LEFT / ANGLE_RIGHT
parameters.description: Row angled left / right of the route direction.

parameters.name: STAGGER
parameters.description: Staggered vias.

tools.notes: Also in the ROUTEMULTI parameter toolbar or via ASSIGN. Related: ROUTEMULTI.

tools.name: SET Ripup_mode
tools.description: Selects the mode of the RIPUP command (also available in its parameter toolbar): what a click rips up, from a single segment to all connected copper, a whole signal, the traces between two parts, all polygons or everything.

parameters.name: DEFAULT | 0
parameters.description: Normal: segment to airwire, polygon to outline, remove a via.

parameters.name: SIGNAL | 1
parameters.description: All traces with the same signal name as the clicked one.

parameters.name: CONNECTED | 2
parameters.description: All copper connected to the clicked segment.

parameters.name: CONNECTED_SAME_LAYER | 3
parameters.description: Connected copper on the same layer only.

parameters.name: ELEMENT_ELEMENT | 4
parameters.description: Click two parts: traces shared between them.

parameters.name: ALL / ALL_POLYGONS
parameters.description: All traces of the design / all polygons back to outline mode.

tools.notes: Related: RIPUP.

tools.name: SET Cmd.* parameters (Cmd.Copy.ClassicEagleMode, Cmd.Delete.WireJointsWithoutCtrl, Cmd.Name.RenameEntireNetByDefault, Cmd.Name.RenameEntireSignalByDefault, Cmd.Wire.IgnoreCtrlForRadiusMode)
tools.description: eaglerc switches that change the default behavior of individual commands; they are not in any dialog and are set with SET using the exact, case-sensitive name and 0 or 1.

parameters.name: Cmd.Copy.ClassicEagleMode
parameters.description: 1 restores the pre-version-6 COPY (copy within the drawing, no clipboard) and CUT behavior; takes effect for the next editor window opened.

parameters.name: Cmd.Delete.WireJointsWithoutCtrl
parameters.description: 1 lets DELETE remove wire joints without holding Ctrl.

parameters.name: Cmd.Name.RenameEntireNetByDefault
parameters.description: 1: NAME renames the entire net/bus instead of only the selected segment.

parameters.name: Cmd.Name.RenameEntireSignalByDefault
parameters.description: 1: NAME on a signal polygon renames the entire signal instead of only the polygon.

parameters.name: Cmd.Wire.IgnoreCtrlForRadiusMode
parameters.description: 1 turns off the Ctrl-click arc radius mode in all wire drawing commands.

tools.notes: Names must be written in full and exactly as shown (case sensitive). Related: COPY, CUT, DELETE, NAME, LINE.

tools.name: SET Interface.* parameters (MouseButtonReleaseTimeout, PreferredUnit, UseCtrlForPanning, VectorFont)
tools.description: eaglerc switches for the user interface: toolbar button release timing, preferred units in dialog fields, the old Ctrl-key panning and forced vector font display.

parameters.name: Interface.MouseButtonReleaseTimeout
parameters.description: Milliseconds within which a button release outside the button still triggers it; default 500, 0 turns it off (if 0 at program start, changes apply only after a restart).

parameters.name: Interface.PreferredUnit
parameters.description: Units shown in dialog fields: 0 automatic (fewest decimals, default), 1 imperial, 2 metric.

parameters.name: Interface.UseCtrlForPanning
parameters.description: 1 pans with the Ctrl key as in old versions instead of the center button/wheel (may conflict with Ctrl functions such as selecting at the origin in MOVE).

parameters.name: Interface.VectorFont
parameters.description: 1 always displays and prints texts with the built-in vector font ('Always vector font').

tools.notes: Related: SET VECTOR_FONT (per drawing), TEXT.

tools.name: SET Option.LayerSequence
tools.description: Defines the order in which layers are rendered, which matters for printers, PDF and PostScript where layers are not transparent; for example user-defined layers can be rendered before internal ones. The value is a string of layer numbers or ranges, each optionally followed by t (only when viewed from top) or b (only when viewed from bottom/mirrored), with * standing for the default internal sequence.

parameters.name: 123 / 123t / 123b
parameters.description: Render layer 123 always / only when viewed from top / only when viewed from bottom.
Ranges in the given order.
Insert the default sequence of the internal layers.

tools.notes: The example makes layer 123 always render first. Viewed from top the sequence is rendered right to left, mirrored left to right; each layer is rendered only once, and unlisted layers follow in ascending order. The default internal sequence starts 48t 49t 19t 47t 20t 46t 23 27 25 ... 1-16 ... 61-99 (full list in the SET help).

tools.name: SET Option.RatsnestLimit
tools.description: Limits how many connection points of a signal RATSNEST processes with all wire end points, to cap memory use (up to the square of the value in bytes). By default all points are processed.

parameters.description: No limit (current default behavior).
The method of older versions.
Airwires connect only to pads, smds and vias.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: All wire end points are used up to n connection points; e.g. 1024 limits memory to about 1 MB.

tools.notes: Only needed on systems where very complex signals exhaust memory. Related: RATSNEST.

tools.name: SET Option.* display parameters (ShowPartOrigins, ShowTextOrigins, SignalNamesOnPads, SignalNamesOnTraces, ViaLength, DrawUnprocessedPolygonEdgesContinuous, UnpopulatedMarkScaling)
tools.description: eaglerc switches that change what the editor draws: origin crosses of parts and texts, signal names on pads and traces, via layer spans, how unprocessed polygon edges look, and the size of the not-populated mark of assembly variants.

parameters.name: Option.ShowPartOrigins / ShowTextOrigins
parameters.description: Small crosses at part (schematic) and text origins; 0 turns them off.

parameters.name: Option.SignalNamesOnPads / SignalNamesOnTraces
parameters.description: Signal name drawn on contacts / on signal wires in the Unrouted layer color; default 1.

parameters.name: Option.ViaLength
parameters.description: 1 displays the layer span on each via; default 0.

parameters.name: Option.DrawUnprocessedPolygonEdgesContinuous
parameters.description: 1 draws unprocessed polygon edges as continuous (not highlighted) lines instead of dotted.

parameters.name: Option.UnpopulatedMarkScaling
parameters.description: Scale of the X mark of unpopulated parts; default 1.0.

tools.notes: A window refresh (WINDOW;) may be needed after changing display parameters. Related: VIA, POLYGON, VARIANT.

tools.name: SET Option.* editing behavior (AutoLoadMatchingDrawingFile, RepositionMouseCursorAfterContextMenu, ToggleCtrlForGroupSelectionAndContextMenu) and ControlPanel.View.AutoOpenProjectFolder
tools.description: eaglerc switches for loading and mouse behavior: automatically loading the matching board/schematic, putting the cursor back after a context menu, swapping group selection and context menu between Right and Ctrl+Right, and auto-opening the project folder in the Control Panel.

parameters.name: Option.AutoLoadMatchingDrawingFile
parameters.description: 1 loads the matching schematic/board without asking when another drawing is loaded while both editors are open.

parameters.name: Option.RepositionMouseCursorAfterContextMenu
parameters.description: 1 moves the cursor back to where it was before a context menu opened.

parameters.name: Option.ToggleCtrlForGroupSelectionAndContextMenu
parameters.description: 1 restores the old scheme: groups selected with the right button alone, context menu with Ctrl+Right.

parameters.name: ControlPanel.View.AutoOpenProjectFolder
parameters.description: 0 stops the project folder from opening automatically at start or on project activation.

tools.notes: Names are case sensitive and must be written in full.

tools.name: SET Sch.*, Erc.* and Warning.* parameters
tools.description: eaglerc switches for schematic defaults, ERC consistency override and individual warning messages: always using the device name as value, group annotation display, forcing forward/back annotation on slightly inconsistent pairs, and suppressing specific warnings.

parameters.name: Sch.Cmd.Add.AlwaysUseDeviceNameAsValue
parameters.description: 1 uses the device name as part value even for parts that need a user value.

parameters.name: Sch.GroupAnnotations
parameters.description: 0 off, 1 on, 2 on hover only (same as SET GROUP_ANNOTATIONS).

parameters.name: Erc.AllowUserOverrideConsistencyCheck
parameters.description: 1 enables a dialog to force forward/back annotation even though ERC finds the files inconsistent (at your own risk; files can be corrupted).

parameters.name: Warning.Cam.DrillsAndHolesConcurrent
parameters.description: 0 suppresses the CAM warning about one file for drills and holes.

parameters.name: Warning.PartHasNoUserDefinableValue
parameters.description: 0 suppresses the warning that a part has no user-definable value.

parameters.name: Warning.SupplyPinAutoOverwriteGeneratedNetName
parameters.description: 1 disables the warning when a supply pin overwrites a generated (N$) net name.

tools.notes: Note the inverted logic of the last parameter (1 disables its warning). Use Erc.AllowUserOverrideConsistencyCheck only as a last resort; the help explicitly warns about possible data loss.
